cards.text: Friend, this one's short, but it hits HARD. A man with leprosy comes to Jesus. He drops to his knees, and he starts begging.

cards.question: The leper on his knees begs Jesus to make him ___.

cards.text: Now listen to HOW he asks. He's already sure Jesus CAN do it. His 'if' is about something else.

cards.question: The leper is sure Jesus can make him clean. What is his 'if' about?

cards.text: Jesus looks at this man down on his knees, and He is moved with compassion.

cards.question: Moved with compassion, Jesus heals the leper from a distance, without touching him.

cards.text: Jesus reaches out His hand and touches the man. “I am willing,” He says. “Be clean!”

cards.question: When Jesus tells the leper “Be clean!” the leprosy leaves him right away.

cards.text: IMMEDIATELY the leprosy leaves him, and the man is cleansed. I waited YEARS in a junk drawer for somebody to open it, and this man waits ZERO seconds.
No hanging around. Jesus promptly sends the man away, with a stern warning on his way out.

cards.question: Jesus sends the healed man away with a stern warning. What is the warning?
Jesus tells the healed man to go show himself to the ___ and present the offering ___ prescribed for his cleansing.

cards.text: Two instructions, nice and clear: keep quiet, and go see the priest. Then the man walks out the door.

cards.question: The healed man keeps the news to himself, just like Jesus told him.

cards.text: Nope. He goes out and openly proclaims it and spreads the news. Honestly, if somebody pulled ME out of that junk drawer, I'd have told the DUST.

cards.question: Now that the healed man is spreading the news, what changes for Jesus?

answers.text: He can't enter a town in plain view
He can't preach in the synagogues
He has to cross the sea by boat

cards.question: So Jesus stays out in solitary places. What happens out there?

answers.text: People come to Him from every quarter
He finally gets some time alone
The priests come out to question Him

cards.text: Jesus stays out in solitary places, and people STILL come to Him from every quarter. That's like turning your phone off and finding the whole group chat standing on your porch.

findings.problem: Card 9 adds nothing new to the passage. It retells the immediate healing that card 8 just asked about and confirmed, then adds a joke, so it works as a recap card.

The joke says he 'waited YEARS in a junk drawer for somebody to open it.' In his backstory the drawer opened many times: people dug through it for scissors or tape, and everyone held their breath each time the light came in. What he waited for was to be remembered and put back to work, not for the drawer to open. The line changes his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Don't go near the priest' brings up the priest right before card 12 asks the baker to fill in 'priest.' This tips off a later answer. Card 4's wrong answer 'Whether the priest will agree' does the same.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Aaron' is a wrong option for the second blank, but the leprosy laws in Leviticus 13:1 were given 'to Moses and Aaron.' A baker could argue that Aaron fits the offering prescribed for cleansing.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Most of card 13 recaps instructions cards 11 and 12 just tested. Its only new beat is the man going out.
'Two instructions, nice and clear: keep quiet, and go see the priest' leaves out the third instruction in Mark 1:44, presenting the offering Moses prescribed. The count he points out isn't accurate.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Card 18 only retells the answers to cards 16 and 17 (solitary places, people coming from every quarter) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The story group is none, so it isn't the 'story isn't over' line either.
